newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk cabinet ignores minister's crime boss scandal.
newsitem.headline: Turk cabinet ignores minister's crime boss scandal.

text.p: The Turkish cabinet on Thursday ignored a scandal swirling round Interior Minister Mehmet Agar, who newspapers said might resign over alleged links between police and organised crime.

"We did not discuss this issue. And we did not discuss the accident in Susurluk," Environment Minister Ziyattin Tokar told reporters after a cabinet meeting during which Agar was widely expected to hand in his resignation.

Agar is at the centre of a scandal that has unravelled since a police chief, a wanted gangster and a former beauty queen died in the same car in a traffic accident last weekend in the western town of Susurluk.

Agar cut short a visit to southeast Turkey to return to Ankara earlier on Thursday. Police in the southeastern city of Diyarbakir said Agar had cancelled a series of engagements to fly to the capital.

A government MP who runs a Kurdish tribal militia that fights separatist guerrillas in the southeast was in the car and is now seriously injured in hospital. Emergency services found pistols and silencers in the vehicle.

"This incident is very serious. It must be taken as far as it will go," President Suleyman Demirel was quoted by the state-run Anatolian news agency as saying. "But you should not draw conclusions about Turkey from this."

A left-wing party has called for a parliamentary censure motion against Agar for failing to clear up the link between the police chief and Abdullah Catli, a mobster wanted in connection with heroin smuggling and political killings.
"The triangle of police, Mafia and politics had brought Interior Minister Mehmet Agar to the brink of resignation," the Milliyet daily said on Wednesday.

The Turkish press has quoted Agar, a member of Tansu Ciller's conservative True Path Party (DYP), as saying the policeman and MP were taking Catli to Istanbul to be arrested when the crash happened. Agar later said his comments had been misunderstood.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, an Islamist in coalition with Ciller, has made no public statement on the scandal.
